tr-deer.front: Deer track: which way did it walk, and what are the 2 small dots behind it?
tr-deer.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 320" font-family="sans-serif">
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="320" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Deer track (front foot)</text>
  <!-- two toes (halves of heart), point = toe tips at top -->
  <path d="M195 70 C180 75 160 110 158 160 C156 200 168 225 185 228 C195 229 197 215 197 200 Z" fill="#6b4f35" stroke="#23261f" stroke-width="2"/>
  <path d="M205 70 C220 75 240 110 242 160 C244 200 232 225 215 228 C205 229 203 215 203 200 Z" fill="#6b4f35" stroke="#23261f" stroke-width="2"/>
  <!-- dewclaws -->
  <ellipse cx="170" cy="262" rx="8" ry="6" fill="#8a9a6b" stroke="#23261f" stroke-width="2"/>
  <ellipse cx="230" cy="262" rx="8" ry="6" fill="#8a9a6b" stroke="#23261f" stroke-width="2"/>
  <!-- direction arrow -->
  <g stroke="#e8590c" stroke-width="4" fill="#e8590c">
    <line x1="320" y1="230" x2="320" y2="90"/>
    <path d="M320 70 L308 94 L332 94 Z"/>
  </g>
  <text x="320" y="252" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="middle">Travel</text>
  <text x="320" y="270" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="middle">direction</text>
  <!-- labels -->
  <line x1="200" y1="66" x2="110" y2="60" stroke="#23261f" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>
  <text x="20" y="56" font-size="14" fill="#23261f">Pointed tips</text>
  <text x="20" y="72" font-size="14" fill="#23261f">= front</text>
  <line x1="160" y1="160" x2="95" y2="160" stroke="#23261f" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>
  <text x="20" y="150" font-size="14" fill="#23261f">2 toes</text>
  <text x="20" y="166" font-size="14" fill="#23261f">(split hoof)</text>
  <line x1="185" y1="228" x2="110" y2="215" stroke="#23261f" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>
  <text x="20" y="210" font-size="14" fill="#23261f">Round heel</text>
  <line x1="162" y1="262" x2="110" y2="270" stroke="#23261f" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>
  <text x="20" y="268" font-size="14" fill="#23261f">Dewclaws:</text>
  <text x="20" y="284" font-size="14" fill="#23261f">deep mud, snow,</text>
  <text x="20" y="300" font-size="14" fill="#23261f">or running</text>
  <text x="200" y="312" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">About 6 to 10 cm long</text>
</svg>
tr-deer.back: The pointed tips point the way it walked. The 2 dots are dewclaws, which show in soft mud, snow or when running.

tr-hare-vs-deer-browse.front: A twig is bitten off. Clean 45 degree cut, or ragged and torn. Who ate it?
tr-hare-vs-deer-browse.back: Clean angled cut: hare or rabbit (they have upper incisors). Ragged, torn tip: deer, moose or elk (no upper front teeth, they tear).
